question: Does the prior unsealed checkpoint show GPU versus CPU inference disagreement on the first sixteen already-consumed completed training groups?
scope: One separately frozen, gradient-free diagnostic; existing training cache and checkpoint only. Neither a fit retry nor an evaluation of the held-out panel.
selection: First 16 completed_observed groups in saved training cache order, no replacement; at most 8192 candidate rows.
comparison: GPU and CPU use the same saved parameters and normalization. Compare all logits at atol=1e-4 and rtol=1e-5 and canonical first argmax for each group. Complete all 16 groups even if ordinary numeric disagreement occurs; report aggregates only.
budget: One WSL GPU process, at most 16 complete group-level GPU forwards, 8192 candidate rows, 300 seconds work and 420 seconds process; no gradients, model fitting, official transition or new game.
identity: Bind prior public failure acceptance and training summary, checkpoint/cache/schema and private GPU launch configuration by SHA256 before decoding model or cache; previous source, default Bot and historical data remain unchanged.
failure: Failure stops without retry; retain phase, last synchronized group counts and bounded private logs. Ordinary numerical mismatch is a valid diagnostic result, not an execution failure.
interpretation: Neither passing nor failing this comparison uniquely identifies the old ValueError or proves game strength, GPU training completion, or a model ready for deployment.
privacy: Do not publish model weights, feature arrays, logits, private configuration, raw replay, paths, logs or individual samples.
